legend: There are n%%ZSMJ0%% people in a row. The height of the i%%ZSMJ1%%-th person is ai%%ZSMJ2%%. You can choose any subset of these people and try to arrange them into a balanced circle.

A balanced circle is such an order of people that the difference between heights of any adjacent people is no more than 1%%ZSMJ3%%. For example, let heights of chosen people be [ai1,ai2,…,aik]%%ZSMJ4%%, where k%%ZSMJ5%% is the number of people you choose. Then the condition |aij−aij+1|≤1%%ZSMJ6%% should be satisfied for all j%%ZSMJ7%% from 1%%ZSMJ8%% to k−1%%ZSMJ9%% and the condition |ai1−aik|≤1%%ZSMJ10%% should be also satisfied. |x|%%ZSMJ11%% means the absolute value of x%%ZSMJ12%%. It is obvious that the circle consisting of one person is balanced.

Your task is to choose the maximum number of people and construct a balanced circle consisting of all chosen people. It is obvious that the circle consisting of one person is balanced so the answer always exists.
input: The first line of the input contains one integer n%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ14%%) — the number of people.
The second line of the input contains n%%ZSMJ15%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ16%% (1≤ai≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ17%%), where ai%%ZSMJ18%% is the height of the i%%ZSMJ19%%-th person.
output: In the first line of the output print k%%ZSMJ20%% — the number of people in the maximum balanced circle.

In the second line print k%%ZSMJ21%% integers res1,res2,…,resk%%ZSMJ22%%, where resj%%ZSMJ23%% is the height of the j%%ZSMJ24%%-th person in the maximum balanced circle. The condition |resj−resj+1|≤1%%ZSMJ25%% should be satisfied for all j%%ZSMJ26%% from 1%%ZSMJ27%% to k−1%%ZSMJ28%% and the condition |res1−resk|≤1%%ZSMJ29%% should be also satisfied.
